title: Euler's Formula and Identity
author: Leonhard Euler
text: For real x, Euler's formula states exp(i x) = cos(x) + i sin(x). At x = pi, this yields exp(i pi) + 1 = 0, relating the fundamental constants 0, 1, pi, e, and i.

title: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
author: Isaac Newton and Gottfried Leibniz
text: If f is continuous on [a,b] and F(x) = integral from a to x of f(t) dt, then F'(x) = f(x). If F is an antiderivative of f, then integral from a to b of f(x) dx = F(b) - F(a).

title: Eigenvalues and Characteristic Polynomial
author: Linear Algebra Reference
text: A scalar lambda is an eigenvalue of a square matrix A if there is a nonzero vector v with A v = lambda v. Eigenvalues are roots of the characteristic polynomial det(A - lambda I).

title: First Isomorphism Theorem
author: Abstract Algebra Reference
text: For a group homomorphism phi: G -> H, the quotient group G / ker(phi) is isomorphic to im(phi). The map g ker(phi) -> phi(g) is well-defined and bijective.

title: Taylor's Theorem
author: Analysis Reference
text: If f has n+1 derivatives near a, f(x) = sum from k=0 to n of f^(k)(a)/k! times (x-a)^k plus a remainder. For analytic functions the Taylor series converges to f within its radius of convergence.

title: Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality
author: Analysis Reference
text: For vectors u and v in an inner product space, the absolute value of the inner product of u and v is at most the product of their norms. Equality holds exactly when u and v are linearly dependent.

title: Rank-Nullity Theorem
author: Linear Algebra Reference
text: For a linear map T from a finite-dimensional vector space V to W, dim(V) equals rank(T) plus nullity(T). The image and kernel dimensions account for every degree of freedom in the domain.

title: Mean Value Theorem
author: Calculus Reference
text: If f is continuous on the closed interval [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b), there exists c in (a,b) such that f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a). The theorem converts a global average rate into a local derivative.

title: Bayes Theorem
author: Probability Reference
text: For events A and B with positive probability, P(A given B) = P(B given A) P(A) / P(B). The denominator can be expanded by the law of total probability when B has multiple causes.

title: Fourier Transform Pair
author: Applied Mathematics Reference
text: The Fourier transform represents a suitable function in frequency space: F(omega) = integral over the real line of f(t) exp(-i omega t) dt. Differentiation in time becomes multiplication by i omega.

title: Fundamental Theorem of Finite Abelian Groups
author: Algebra Reference
text: Every finite abelian group is isomorphic to a direct product of cyclic groups of prime-power order. The invariant factors or elementary divisors determine the decomposition up to isomorphism.

title: Markov Inequality
author: Probability Reference
text: For a nonnegative random variable X and a positive number a, P(X >= a) <= E[X]/a. It follows by comparing the indicator of the event X >= a with X/a.
